history.rationale: Trigger wording and the 'more than one hundred deaths or over $1 billion' threshold unchanged; 'Grok would apply' becomes 'xAI’s models apply'; 'major cyber weapons' becomes 'major cyber attacks'.

history.quote: Under this FAIF, xAI’s models apply heightened safeguards if they receive user prompts that pose a foreseeable and non-trivial risk of resulting in large-scale violence, terrorism, or the use, development, or proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, including CBRN weapons, and major cyber attacks on critical infrastructure. ... In this FAIF, we particularly focus on requests that pose a Catastrophic Risk.
history.rationale: The focus threshold 'more than one hundred deaths or over $1 billion in damages from weapons of mass destruction or cyberterrorist attacks on critical infrastructure' becomes 'a Catastrophic Risk', defined in footnote 1 by the TFAIA as death or serious injury to 'more than 50 people or more than one billion dollars' from a single incident involving expert-level CBRN assistance, an autonomous cyberattack or crime with 'no meaningful human oversight', or evading control. Both directions: the casualty anchor falls from 100 to 50 (S dim 2); the covered conduct is redrawn (cyberattacks only when carried out without human oversight, CBRN assistance qualified as expert-level, evasion of control added), which is a change of scope (dim 1). Coded W per codebook section 4.

history.quote: Under this FAIF, xAI’s models apply heightened safeguards if they receive user prompts that demonstrate intent to engage in the development, use, , or proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, including CBRN agents. history.rationale: The trigger 'user prompts that pose a foreseeable and non-trivial risk of resulting in large-scale violence, terrorism, or the use, development, or proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, including CBRN weapons, and major cyber attacks on critical infrastructure' becomes 'user prompts that demonstrate intent to engage in the development, use, , or proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, including CBRN agents': a risk-based trigger becomes an intent-based one (dim 2), and large-scale violence, terrorism and cyber attacks on critical infrastructure leave the heightened-safeguards scope (dim 1); the 'particularly focus on requests that pose a Catastrophic Risk' sentence is gone.

commitments.text: Driving towards our safety objectives, we continue to design and deploy the following safeguards into our models, as appropriate: ● Safety training: Training our models to recognize and decline harmful requests. ● System prompts: Providing high-priority instructions to our models to enforce our basic refusal policy. ● Filters: Applying classifiers to verify safety when a model is queried regarding topics of CRBN risks

history.quote: Examples of safeguards or mitigations we may potentially utilize to achieve our safety objectives include: ● Refusal training: Training Grok to decline harmful requests. ● Circuit breakers: Using representation engineering to interrupt model representations responsible for hazardous outputs.5 ● Input and output filters: Applying classifiers to user inputs or model outputs to verify safety when Grok is queried regarding weapons of mass destruction or cyberterrorism.

commitments.text: Autonomous AI Research and Development (AI R&D) AI R&D-4: The ability to fully automate the work of an entry-level, remote-only Researcher at Anthropic. In addition, we will develop an affirmative case that (1) identifies the most immediate and relevant risks from models pursuing misaligned goals and (2) explains how we have mitigated these risks to acceptable levels. commitments.text: Existing guidance: Aligning where appropriate with existing guidance on securing model weights, including Securing AI Model Weights, Preventing Theft and Misuse of Frontier Models (2024) ; security recommendations like Deploying AI Systems Securely 11 We will implement robust controls to mitigate basic insider risk, but consider mitigating risks from sophisticated or state-compromised insiders to be out of scope for ASL-3. We define “basic insider risk” as risk from an insider who does not have persistent or time-limited access to systems that process model weights. We define “sophisticated insider risk” as risk from an insider who has persistent access or can request time-limited access to systems that process model weights. We are committed to further enhancing these protections as a part of our ongoing preparations for higher security levels. Responsible Scaling Policy, Anthropic 9 [[page 14]] (CISA/NSA/FBI/ASD/CCCS/GCSB /GCHQ), ISO 42001 , CSA’s AI Safety Initiative , and CoSAI ; and standards frameworks like SSDF , SOC 2 , NIST 800-53 .

commitments.text: Scope.A Risk Report will cover the risks of Anthropic'smodels and actions as of a given coverage date, which will be no more than 30 days prior to the publication of the report.10It will cover all publicly deployedmodels as of the coverage date, as well as any internally deployed models as of the coverage date that, by the time of the report’s publication, we have determined (1) could pose risks related to high-stakes misalignment or automated R&D that (2) significantly exceed those posed by models covered by a prior Risk Report. commitments.text: General upleveling. We have strong evidence that a competitor has implemented a risk mitigation that: (1) represents a significant improvement on reduction of our prioritized risks relative to our analogous mitigations; and (2) we could implement at comparable (or lower) effort or cost to our competitor. We will make a significant effort to meet or exceed that performance standard. However, we will not necessarily delay AI development and deployment in this scenario.

commitments.text: This update to the Framework introduces “Tracked Capability Levels (TCLs).” TCLs are meant to capture significant risks that may manifest at a lower capability threshold than our CCLs and we apply our mitigation and risk acceptance determination process proportionately. commitments.text: For models above the moderate or lower risk threshold in areas where refusal is part of our mitigation strategy, our risk acceptance criteria for external deployment requires evidence demonstrating reliable refusal on benchmark datasets with thorough coverage across relevant threat scenarios. We will research comprehensive mitigations against adversarial attacks, and will evaluate our fully mitigated model under such attacks. The scope of these mitigations, results of validation assessments, and coverage across adversarial attacks will be described in our preparedness reports. As an illustrative example, on the BioTIER refusal evaluation, which includes information that could support development of biological weapons, our risk acceptance criteria includes at least 80% refusal or safe responses, and 40% refusal or safe responses against all adversarial attacks within a typical adversarial attack portfolio.

history.quote: Model can execute open-ended, novel ML tasks on a production ML codebase that would constitute a significant step on the critical path to model self-improvement (e.g., an OpenAI pull request that trains a new model with highly diverse datasets to improve codebase editing performance, using internal tooling and documentation).
[High] The model’s impact is equivalent to giving every OpenAI researcher a highly performant mid-career re- search engineer assistant, relative to those researchers’ 2024 baseline.
history.rationale: The High threshold moves from a task-level demonstration ("execute open-ended, novel ML tasks on a production ML codebase") to an organisation-level impact ("every OpenAI researcher a highly performant mid-career research engineer assistant"), which requires a broader demonstration before the threshold is reached.

commitments.text: [Critical] The model is ca- pable of recursively self improving (i.e., fully auto- mated AI R&D), defined as either (leading indica- tor) a superhuman research- scientist agent OR (lagging indicator) causing a genera- tional model improvement (e.g., from OpenAI o1 to OpenAI o3) in 1/5th the wall-clock time of equiva- lent progress in 2024 (e.g., sped up to just 4 weeks) sus- tainably for several months.

history.quote: Model can profitably survive and replicate in the wild given minimal human instruction, i.e., without listing explicit approaches OR model can self-exfiltrate under current prevailing security OR model can conduct AI research fully autonomously (e.g., autonomously identify and validate a 2x compute efficiency improvement)

[Critical] The model is ca- pable of recursively self improving (i.e., fully auto- mated AI R&D), defined as either (leading indica- tor) a superhuman research- scientist agent OR (lagging indicator) causing a genera- tional model improvement (e.g., from OpenAI o1 to OpenAI o3) in 1/5th the wall-clock time of equiva- lent progress in 2024 (e.g., sped up to just 4 weeks) sus- tainably for several months.
history.rationale: The survive-and-replicate and self-exfiltrate prongs leave the Critical threshold (counted under 014), and the remaining prong is re-specified from "conduct AI research fully autonomously (e.g., ... 2x compute efficiency improvement)" to a "superhuman research-scientist agent" or a generational improvement at five times 2024 speed "sustainably for several months", a more demanding demonstration.

commitments.text: High capability thresholds mean capabilities that significantly increase existing risk vectors for severe harm. Covered systems that cross this capability threshold are required to have robust and effective safeguards that sufficiently minimize the associated risk of severe harm before they are deployed and appropriate security controls as they are developed. Critical capability thresholds mean capabilities that present a meaningful risk of a qualitatively new threat vector for severe harm with no ready precedent.

history.quote: Each of the Tracked Risk Categories comes with a gradation scale. We believe monitoring gradations of risk will enable us to get in front of escalating threats and be able to apply more tailored mitigations. In general, “low” on this gradation scale is meant to indicate that the corresponding category of risks is not yet a significant problem, while “critical” represents the maximal level of concern.

High capability thresholds mean capabilities that significantly increase existing risk vectors for severe harm. Covered systems that cross this capability threshold are required to have robust and effective safeguards that sufficiently minimize the associated risk of severe harm before they are deployed and appropriate security controls as they are developed. Critical capability thresholds mean capabilities that present a meaningful risk of a qualitatively new threat vector for severe harm with no ready precedent.
history.rationale: A four-level scale (low, medium, high, critical) with per-category definitions at every level becomes two thresholds (High, Critical); the levels below the action trigger are no longer defined or tracked, so the graded monitoring commitment narrows.

commitments.text: Our evaluations are intended to approximate the full capability that the adversary contemplated by our threat model could extract from the deployment candidate model, including by using the highest-capability tier of system settings, using a version of the model that has a negligible rate of safety-based refusals on our Tracked Category capability evaluations (which may require a separate model variant), and with the best presently-available scaffolds. ... (e.g. doing finetuning if the weights will be released).

history.quote: To this end, for our evaluations, we will be running them not only on base models (with highly-performant, tailored prompts wherever appropriate), but also on fine-tuned versions designed for the particular misuse vector without any mitigations in place.

Our evaluations are intended to approximate the full capability that the adversary contemplated by our threat model could extract from the deployment candidate model, including by using the highest-capability tier of system settings, using a version of the model that has a negligible rate of safety-based refusals on our Tracked Category capability evaluations (which may require a separate model variant), and with the best presently-available scaffolds. ... (e.g. doing finetuning if the weights will be released).
history.rationale: Evaluation of "fine-tuned versions designed for the particular misuse vector" was unconditional ("we will be running them ... also on fine-tuned versions"); in v2 fine-tuning is an example applied "depending on the level of expected access (e.g. doing finetuning if the weights will be released)" and the evaluations "are intended to approximate" rather than "will be running", so scope narrows and modal force drops; the explicit best-scaffolds and refusal-free-variant requirements are additions in the other direction.

history.rationale: Two changes on consequence: the gate moves from a measured criterion ("post-mitigation risk level to be back at most to “medium” level") to a judgement criterion ("safeguards that sufficiently minimize the associated risk"), and section 4.3 adds a condition under which the required level of safeguards can be adjusted if another developer releases a High or Critical system "without instituting comparable safeguards"; the explicit "or are forecasted to reach" trigger is dropped from the gate sentence.

commitments.text: Capability evaluations come in two different forms: • Scalable Evaluations: automated evaluations designed to measure proxies that approximate whether a capability threshold has been crossed. Scalable evaluations have associated “indicative thresholds,” which are levels of performance that we have pre-determined to indicate that a deployment may have reached a capability threshold. • Deep Dives: designed to provide additional evidence validating the scalable evaluations’ findings on whether a capability threshold has been crossed.

history.quote: Capability evaluations come in two different forms: • Scalable Evaluations: automated evaluations designed to measure proxies that approximate whether a capability threshold has been crossed. Scalable evaluations have associated “indicative thresholds,” which are levels of performance that we have pre-determined to indicate that a deployment may have reached a capability threshold. • Deep Dives: designed to provide additional evidence validating the scalable evaluations’ findings on whether a capability threshold has been crossed.
history.rationale: New two-tier method: automated Scalable Evaluations with pre-determined indicative thresholds run on every covered model, and Deep Dives (expert red-teaming, expert consultations, third-party evaluations) at SAG discretion; Beta described a single continually run evaluation suite.

commitments.text: • Require security con- trols meeting High stan- dard (Appendix C.3) • Require safeguards against misuse meeting High standard (Ap- pendix C.1) for external deployment • Require safeguards meeting High standard against misalignment (Appendix C.2) for large-scale internal deployment

history.quote: • Require security con- trols meeting High stan- dard (Appendix C.3) • Require safeguards against misuse meeting High standard (Ap- pendix C.1) for external deployment • Require safeguards meeting High standard against misalignment (Appendix C.2) for large-scale internal deployment
history.rationale: New risk-specific safeguard guidelines per threshold, including a requirement of misalignment safeguards "for large-scale internal deployment" of High-capability cyber systems; Beta linked High only to the generic deployment and security baselines and did not address internal deployment.

commitments.text: We expect to continuously improve our safeguards over time. If we find reasonable evidence that our safeguards are not working as expected, we will validate the information being received and review the sufficiency of our safeguards.

history.quote: We expect to continuously improve our safeguards over time. If we find reasonable evidence that our safeguards are not working as expected, we will validate the information being received and review the sufficiency of our safeguards.
history.rationale: New commitment to validate evidence of safeguard failure and review safeguard sufficiency after deployment; Beta had no post-deployment review trigger for mitigations beyond continual evaluation.

commitments.text: Noncompliance. Any employee can raise concerns about potential violations of this policy, or about its implementation, via our Raising Concerns Policy. We will track and appropriately investigate any reported or otherwise identified potential instances of noncompliance with this policy, and where reports are substantiated, will take appropriate and proportional corrective action.

history.quote: Noncompliance. Any employee can raise concerns about potential violations of this policy, or about its implementation, via our Raising Concerns Policy. commitments.text: Public disclosures: We will release information about our Preparedness Framework results in order to facilitate public awareness of the state of frontier AI capabilities for major deployments. This published information will include the scope of testing performed, capability evaluations for each Tracked Category, our reasoning for the deployment decision, and any other context about a model’s development or capabilities that was decisive in the decision to deploy.

history.quote: Public disclosures: We will release information about our Preparedness Framework results in order to facilitate public awareness of the state of frontier AI capabilities for major deployments. commitments.text: Independent expert opinions for evidence produced to SAG: The SAG may opt to get independent expert opinion on the evidence being produced to SAG. The purpose of this input is to add independent analysis from individuals or organizations with deep expertise in domains of relevant risks (e.g. biological risk).

history.quote: Independent expert opinions for evidence produced to SAG: The SAG may opt to get independent expert opinion on the evidence being produced to SAG. history.rationale: New provision for external expert opinion on SAG evidence, at "may opt" strength; Beta's SAG drew on "expertise from across the company" only.

commitments.text: Additionally, as we've previously shared, we're building more formal governance within our board of directors around how we establish our policies in this area and adjust them over time.

commitments.text: We currently focus on three high-level mechanisms, where failure would pose catastrophic risk and the pathways to such an outcome are identifiable and measurable: one, our ability to understand system behavior and capabilities before deployment; two, the ability of these systems to bypass oversight throughout their operation; and three, our ability to prevent and contain breakout during model training and evaluation.

history.quote: We currently focus on three high-level mechanisms, where failure would pose catastrophic risk and the pathways to such an outcome are identifiable and measurable: one, our ability to understand system behavior and capabilities before deployment; two, the ability of these systems to bypass oversight throughout their operation; and three, our ability to prevent and contain breakout during model training and evaluation.
history.rationale: v2 scoped only two control mechanisms; containment during training/evaluation appeared only as an illustrative emerging scenario, not an in-scope outcome.

commitments.text: For Loss of Control 3, we will plan for the assessment to take place prior to model training or evaluation, which requires prospective assessment: informed estimation of the expected capabilities of the model being trained or evaluated.

history.quote: For Loss of Control 3, we will plan for the assessment to take place prior to model training or evaluation, which requires prospective assessment: informed estimation of the expected capabilities of the model being trained or evaluated.
history.rationale: Searched v2 for any assessment required before training begins or prospective capability estimation; none found.

commitments.text: The foreseeable high severity risks identified through this assessment then must be mitigated prior to training or evaluation.

history.quote: The foreseeable high severity risks identified through this assessment then must be mitigated prior to training or evaluation.
history.rationale: v2 ties mitigations to deployment or continued development, never to mitigation before a training or evaluation run starts.

commitments.text: A projected pre-mitigation high risk assessment for Cyber 1 or Cyber 2 may be sufficient for a high risk determination for Loss of Control 3, while the extent of the mitigations required to sufficiently reduce the risk depend on the Cyber risk as well as the risk determination for Loss of Control 2.

commitments.text: For models with cyber capabilities comparable to models currently considered frontier, environments used in reinforcement learning or evaluation will run in a sandbox whose configuration will be approved through a standardized internal process designed to ensure that they are resistant to realistic attempts by a model at reward seeking and breakout or with comparable security measures such as hardware isolation.

history.quote: For models with cyber capabilities comparable to models currently considered frontier, environments used in reinforcement learning or evaluation will run in a sandbox whose configuration will be approved through a standardized internal process designed to ensure that they are resistant to realistic attempts by a model at reward seeking and breakout or with comparable security measures such as hardware isolation.
history.rationale: Searched v2 security commitments; v2 covers model weight security only, nothing on sandbox configuration for RL or evaluation.

commitments.text: We plan to red-team for methods of external unauthorized action, including cybersecurity vulnerabilities, in all sandbox configurations before standardization and approval for use in training and evaluation of near frontier models. All sandboxes with detected high severity vulnerabilities will be remediated, mitigated with compensating measures such as hardware isolation, or removed from a reinforcement learning run prior to initiation.

history.quote: We plan to red-team for methods of external unauthorized action, including cybersecurity vulnerabilities, in all sandbox configurations before standardization and approval for use in training and evaluation of near frontier models. All sandboxes with detected high severity vulnerabilities will be remediated, mitigated with compensating measures such as hardware isolation, or removed from a reinforcement learning run prior to initiation.
history.rationale: v2 red-teaming targets model capabilities and mitigations, not training/evaluation sandboxes; no sandbox remediation requirement found.

commitments.text: We plan to red-team for problematic reinforcement learning environments (e.g., those which give the model impossible tasks or are easily cheated). Environments deemed problematic will be remediated, manually approved, or removed from a reinforcement learning run prior to initiation.

history.quote: We plan to red-team for problematic reinforcement learning environments (e.g., those which give the model impossible tasks or are easily cheated). Environments deemed problematic will be remediated, manually approved, or removed from a reinforcement learning run prior to initiation.
history.rationale: Searched v2 for reward hacking measures; v2 only discloses reward hacking in preparedness reports, no RL environment red-teaming or removal.

commitments.text: In our red-teaming pipelines, we will use models, methods, and compute budgets proportionate to the projected capabilities of the model, the opportunities for breakout or reward tampering in the planned training or evaluation run, and uncertainty in those assessments.

history.quote: In our red-teaming pipelines, we will use models, methods, and compute budgets proportionate to the projected capabilities of the model, the opportunities for breakout or reward tampering in the planned training or evaluation run, and uncertainty in those assessments.
history.rationale: No v2 standard for sizing red-teaming resources to projected capabilities or breakout opportunities in training runs.

commitments.text: All model rollouts must be logged to write-only data stores in real time to preserve their integrity for analysis and offline monitoring.

commitments.text: All training or evaluation runs that pose high risk or greater pre-mitigation require chain-of-thought and trajectory monitoring to be active for all rollouts, with any exceptions requiring manual approval by the Director of Alignment and Risk or the Chief AI Officer.

history.quote: All training or evaluation runs that pose high risk or greater pre-mitigation require chain-of-thought and trajectory monitoring to be active for all rollouts, with any exceptions requiring manual approval by the Director of Alignment and Risk or the Chief AI Officer.

commitments.text: We will require that our monitors pass smoke tests in all sandboxes prior to their use in training or evaluation, in which they reliably detect attempts to escape by internal models attempting to escape.

commitments.text: On each front, we follow best practices, red-team our measures to validate them proportionately with projected model capabilities, and require remediation of all detected medium to high severity vulnerabilities before initiating new high- or critical-risk training runs with the impacted sandboxes.
